thread:
incident-bot: Pager triggered: runtime pool 'r13' - evictions spike, 5 OOMs in last 5m. @elena you are oncall. Severity: S1 -> escalate if impact continues

elena: on it. joining now. any customer-impact notes?

support-lead: seeing ~12 customers with >10s tails, 3 customers with 5xxs. dashboard: https://redwood.internal/alerts/3412345678

mike: quick hypothesis: large-batch requests causing KV cache growth + fragmentation. saw similar pattern last month.

jess: uploading filtered runtime logs to s3: s3://redwood-logs/incidents/3412345678/runtime-filtered.log (contains nvidia traces & eviction counters)

thomas: copying relevant snippet from the log (recent evict loop):
```
2026-03-17T15:02:11Z runtime[pid=32412] KVCache::evict_one -> evicted 0 items (checked 128)
2026-03-17T15:02:12Z runtime[pid=32412] allocation failed: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
2026-03-17T15:02:12Z runtime[pid=32412] batch_size=16 seq_avg=1024 model=m-open-13B
```

kai: running `nvidia-smi` on node r13-02 -> memory used: 39818MiB / 40960MiB, processes: runtime(90%), other 5%

elena: thanks. immediate mitigations: reduce max batch for r13 pool, start draining the 2 brightest nodes from traffic, enable fallback smaller model variant for large inputs. I'll push throttles now.

kai: pushed env change to pool r13: `ROUTING_MAX_BATCH=8` and `FALLBACK_MODEL=m-open-7B` via deploy bot. curl -X POST https://console.internal/pools/r13/update -d '{"max_batch":8}'

infra-bot: Deploy applied: r13 config updated by kai at 2026-03-17T15:06:20Z. Rolling restart scheduled for 30s.

mike: can someone run a heap/profile dump of the runtime process that hit OOM? try: `gcore <pid>` or `python -m tracemalloc` where possible. we need KV cache size distribution.

jess: dropped a filtered pmap+memtrack here: s3://redwood-logs/incidents/3412345678/pmap-kvsize.txt. top entries: kv_cache shards showing 18-24GB each on two processes.

thomas: preliminary hypothesis: KV cache retention bumped due to a spike of long-prefix prompts from a single customer. cache growth + fragmentation -> cudaMalloc failures at high water mark. note: model m-open-13B salted with long-seq contexts.

support-lead: which customers triggered the spike? we should notify them if we need to throttle.

elena: identified customer ids in the log: acct-9a3, acct-c2b. Reached out via status page: https://status.redwood.com/incidents/3412345678/update.

kai: running a quick local reproduce: sending 20 reqs batch=16 seq=2048 to r13, I can reproduce allocation failure within ~90s. lowering batch to 8 avoids OOM.

mike: corroborates. short-term action: keep ROUTING_MAX_BATCH=8, start controlled rollout of a KV cache cap (per-shard) patch in canary to evict older prefixes aggressively. Also consider prefix-length gating (reject > 4096 or route to smaller model).

jess: posted a minimal patch to apply LRU cap on KV shards: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pull/8742 - it's a quick canary build. logs for canary at s3://redwood-logs/incidents/3412345678/canary-run.log

elena: runbook steps executed so far: 1) reduced batch 2) enabled fallback 3) drained 2 nodes 4) canary patch queued. Customer impact trimmed: 5 customers still seeing elevated tails, no new 5xxs in last 6m.

thomas: long-term follow-up items (RCA): - KV cache accounting per-request + metrics - fragmentation-aware allocator or defrag job - smarter routing for long-seq requests - circuit-breaker for per-customer prefix growth

support-lead: drafting customer communication. will ask for opt-in to throttle heavy prefixes or reroute them.

kai: one more datapoint: GPU free memory fragmentation visible in driver: several small free segments totaling ~3.8GB but no single contiguous block >= 6GB needed by model -> causes cudaMalloc to fail despite headroom.

mike: that's the fragmentation angle. try enabling `cudaMallocAsync` fallback or run a defrag/eviction to consolidate. but careful - defrag could spike latency.

elena: decision: keep current mitigations until 15:40, promote canary if green, and schedule a controlled defrag on low-traffic window (02:00 UTC). start RCA doc after postmortem. assigning owners: mike (allocator/defrag), thomas (KV cache changes), jess (logs + timeline), elena (incident lead).

incident-bot: Severity downgraded to S2 at 2026-03-17T15:32:05Z (customer impact reduced).

elena: thanks team. I'll run a short retrospective doc and ping for triage meeting in 1h. if anyone finds new 5xxs, @elena immediately.

mike: saving checkpoints: upload screenshots + metrics to /incidents/3412345678/pack.zip

jess: uploading final timeline (with log offsets) to s3://redwood-logs/incidents/3412345678/timeline.md

support-lead: fine-grained customer updates posted. adding affected customers to private thread for follow-up.

elena: incident paused for live mitigation. RCA doc in progress: https://docs.internal/redwood/incidents/3412345678-rca (will link when ready)

kai: closing my loop on the reproduce. will continue test with defrag heuristics in canary.

infra-bot: note: scheduled defrag job ticket created: INFRA-9987, targeted 2026-03-18 02:00 UTC.

elena: good work everyone :thumbsup:
